title: History
d: Wrigley Field opened in 1914. The ivy; the Friendly Confines..
definition: Wrigley Field opened in 1914. The ivy; the Friendly Confines..
description: The history of Wrigley Field begins in 1914. The ivy; the Friendly Confines. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

title: Architecture
d: Wrigley Field holds about 41,649 spectators in its current configuration.

description: The architecture of Wrigley Field: a 41,649-capacity bowl designed to trap noise and frame the action. Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants
d: Wrigley Field is home to Chicago Cubs.
definition: Wrigley Field is home to Chicago Cubs.
description: Wrigley Field belongs to Chicago Cubs — and to the fans who fill it. The tenant-club bond defines the ground's identity: the songs, the rituals, the expectation. When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

title: Great matches
d: The greatest nights at Wrigley Field live in legend.

title: Finals hosted

definition: Wrigley Field has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
description: Showpiece events at Wrigley Field: cup finals, international tournaments, and one-off spectacles that put the ground on the world stage. Hosting a final is a civic honor — the city dresses up, the world watches, and the stadium joins the short list of venues that have seen it all.

title: Concerts and events
d: Wrigley Field doubles as a concert and event venue.
definition: Wrigley Field doubles as a concert and event venue.
description: Beyond sport, Wrigley Field hosts concerts, ceremonies, and mega-events — the biggest stages need the biggest rooms. The ground's event history reads like pop culture itself. Multi-use keeps the economics working, though purists always prefer the roar of a matchday to anything else.

On matchdays arrive early, learn the songs, and respect the home ends. Chicago, USA is best reached by public transport; driving on event days is for the patient.

title: Best seats

The famous ends have waiting lists measured in years; the family sections trade noise for comfort. Wherever you sit, the rule is the same — arrive early, stay late.

d: Wrigley Field's biggest crowds and what drew them.

title: The future
d: What is next for Wrigley Field.
definition: What is next for Wrigley Field.
